content.title: About
content.content: Hard flavored pretzels are baked wheat‑flour snacks formed into the classic knot shape and baked until a crisp crust forms. After the first bake they are coated with salt and a variety of flavorings (cheese, onion, paprika, garlic, etc.) and baked again to lock in the taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels have a medieval European origin; the modern hard pretzel evolved from the traditional German "Brezel".
Flavorings are applied after the initial bake and the pretzel is finished with a second bake to set the seasoning.
The hard texture makes pretzels ideal for long‑term storage and transport.
In the United States more than 2 billion servings of pretzels are consumed each year.
The iconic knot shape was historically used as a good‑luck symbol by bakers.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels provide starch that supplies steady energy and helps keep you feeling full.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Wheat flour contributes a modest amount of iron, essential for oxygen transport.

items.title: Vitamin B6 content
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports protein metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Unlike many sweet snacks, hard pretzels typically contain little to no added sugar.

items.title: Fiber in whole‑grain versions
items.content: Whole‑grain pretzels add dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Pretzels made from wheat flour can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The salty coating can contribute to excess sodium intake, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: The hard, dense texture means a small serving can contain a notable number of calories.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Hard, crunchy pieces may pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy pretzels as a standalone snack, pair them with cheese, mustard, hummus, or dip sauces. They also add a crunchy element to salads, charcuterie boards, and snack mixes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pretzels in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For extended freshness, store them in the refrigerator to maintain their crispness.
